messages:
alex_support: Heads-up — AcmeCorp opened an escalation. After last night's model rollout (rerank-v2), they're seeing intermittent 5xxs on /v1/rerank and also different ranks for the exact same input. filing now.

maria_cs: reported errors around 02:12 UTC. Customer pasted two request IDs that show 502 then a successful response with a wildly different score set for the same candidates.

alex_support: sample payload customer sent: 
```json
{
  "query": "best running shoes for flat feet",
  "candidates": [ ... 15 items ... ],
  "top_k": 5
}
```
They say they retried same body several times, sometimes 502/504, sometimes 200 with different ordering.

sam_ml: @devon_infra could routing fallback be returning a different model shard variant? also any batching changes in the rollout? :thinking_face:

devon_infra: quick summary from logs: during the window we saw quota spikes for that tenant hitting concurrent-request cap -> requests got queued; some hit the generic 503 path when the queue timed out. There was also an automatic fallback to an older quantized variant (rerank-v1-quant) for capacity reasons. That explains score differences.

alex_support: customer is upset; they said this is breaking search UX. they want repro steps and either a rollback or an SLA credit.

maria_cs: collecting repro artifacts now. asked them to attach: raw request/response (full headers), request-id, and the exact timestamps. Also asked for repeatable cURL they used.

qa_lead: quick repro I ran locally against staging: if you send 10 concurrent rerank requests with candidate lists ~20 items you can reproduce the timeout -> 503 -> fallback variant path. snip of curl: 
```bash
for i in {1..10}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank -d @payload.json & done
```
Response excerpt: 
```
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
X-Request-ID: req_abc123
{ "error": "server_queue_timeout" }
```

sam_ml: important: fallback model is not bit-identical -> ranking calibrations differ. We need to avoid silent fallback for rerank customers sensitive to order.

devon_infra: agreed. immediate remediation: 1) disable automatic fallback for the rerank route for enterprise tenants, 2) increase per-tenant concurrency limits for the short window, 3) rerun a controlled canary to validate. I've started a config patch.

alex_support: billing note — customer also saw unexpected invoice alerts when retries bumped token usage. @billing-bot any thoughts?

billing-bot: The customer exceeded their burst quota during retries which triggered overage billing. I can draft a one-off credit for the disputed invoice if team approves.

maria_cs: status update to customer: apologized, explained it's a capacity/fallback issue causing inconsistent scores and possible extra tokens from retries. asked if they want immediate rollback to rerank-v1 for their tenant while we fix routing.

sam_ml: for long-term: we should add a rerank-specific invariant check in the router: if request includes deterministic flag or tenant is marked "stable-rerank", do not fallback or change model family. Also add a header in responses when model variant differs: X-Model-Variant.

devon_infra: already adding X-Model-Variant to debug logs. rolling the config that blocks fallback for customer-scoped requests now. will post deploy-bot updates.

deploy-bot: config patch applied to prod-rerank-pool-3 at 1719010800, no restarts required.

alex_support: customer accepted temporary rollback to rerank-v1 for their tenant. I requested scoped rollback, no tenant-wide impact.

maria_cs: next actions for triage checklist: 
- capture full request/response sets for the affected window (done)
- confirm billing credit (pending)
- deploy router rule to block fallback (in progress)
- add X-Model-Variant header for visibility (in progress)
- run synthetic regression tests comparing top_k stable ordering between variants (sam_ml)

sam_ml: I'll run the regression harness on the saved inputs and attach a CSV with score deltas. early estimates: ~7% of queries showed rank flips > 0.2 score delta when falling back to quantized variant.

alex_support: thanks everyone. I let customer know we're on it and offered rollback + credit. keeping thread open for postmortem artifacts. :thumbsup:
